method.tiling: complete census: regular 15 x 15 km grid in EPSG:3400 (NAD83 / Alberta 10-TM Forest); every cell intersecting the Natural Earth 1:10m Alberta polygon is a window
method.landcover: ESA WorldCover 2021 at COG overview level 3 (~160 m) resampled (nearest) to 150 m on the window grid; DSM-safe rule tree<=0.10, built<=0.05, crop<=0.20, water<=0.20, wetland+mangrove<=0.10, snow/ice<0.30, valid land>=0.5 (same as earth stage)
method.fingerprint: pipeline.earth.fingerprint.fingerprint_dem on GLO-90 (15.03 km core + 15 km buffer, local UTM, centred on the window centre); identical to the global screen; shadow is the LOCAL proxy shadow_frac_local_el* (window + buffer only, no far field)
method.distance:
(identical to pipeline.earth.rank_stage1.distances; re-implemented here so the Alberta module
does not depend on a file still being edited, and tested against it in tests/test_alberta.py):
- W1(a, b) = mean |Q_a - Q_b| over the 101 quantiles (1-D Wasserstein-1).
- shadow : mean over el 1,3,5 of W1(per-pixel shadowed-azimuth fraction) / max(Moon IQR, 0.05).
- rim    : mean of W1(1 km jump samples) / max(Moon IQR, 10 m) and |frac_track_over_500m diff| / s.
- texture: mean of W1(slope) / max(Moon IQR, 1 deg) and |nu(L) diff| / s for L = 180/360/720/1440 m.
Scalar scales s are the IQR of that metric over the GLOBAL earth screen population
(data/interim/earth/screen_fingerprints.csv, selected_by == global_screen), so Alberta distances are on
exactly the same scale as the global screen. Falls back to the Alberta population if that file is absent.
method.refine: top 5 per region x hazard re-run at 30 m: GLO-30 core 500x500 + 15 km buffer, GLO-90 far field at 180 m to <= 150 km, R_eff = 7/6 R_earth, compute_all (same as earth stage 2)
method.names: GeoNames: '<named terrain feature (class T) within 7.5 km> · <d> km <dir> of <nearest populated place with population >= 500>'
method.parks: CPCAD park-type polygons (national/provincial/wildland parks, wilderness and natural areas, ecological reserves, heritage rangelands, recreation areas); any overlap >= 1 % of a window sets park.label
